skills.name: Apostrophes for belonging
skills.description: 's for one owner, s' for several; never for plurals.

skills.name: its / it's, your / you're, their / they're

ENG_APOS_PLURAL.label: Uses an apostrophe just to make a word plural

ENG_APOS_PLACE.label: Puts the apostrophe in the wrong place for one or several owners
ENG_APOS_PLACE.explanation: Writes 'the girl's coats' for several girls, or 'the dogs' tail' for one dog.

ENG_CONTRACTION_MIX.label: Confuses it's / you're / they're with its / your / their
ENG_CONTRACTION_MIX.explanation: Writes 'the cat licked it's paw' or 'your going to love it'.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence:  The ___ tail was wagging. (one dog)
hints: An apostrophe shows that something belongs to someone. It is NOT used just to make a plural.
One owner: add 's (the dog's tail). Several owners ending in s: add ' after the s (the girls' coats).
solution: One owner: add 's.
The dog's tail was wagging.

apostrophes_for_possession.title: Apostrophes for belonging
apostrophes_for_possession.big_idea: An apostrophe shows that something belongs to someone. It never makes a word plural: six apples, not six apple's. Where it goes depends on whether there is one owner or several.
steps: Ask: does something belong to someone? If not, no apostrophe.
One owner: write the owner, then 's (the dog's tail).
Several owners and the plural ends in s: write the plural, then ' (the girls' coats).
Check by saying 'the tail of the dog' or 'the coats of the girls'.
apostrophes_for_possession.sense_check: 'The teachers' room' is shared by all the teachers; 'the teacher's desk' belongs to one.

worked_examples.prompt: The ___ coats were on the pegs. (several girls)
steps: Already ends in s, so add ': girls'.

contractions_vs_possessives.title: its / it's, your / you're, their / they're
contractions_vs_possessives.big_idea: In it's, you're and they're the apostrophe shows missing letters (it is, you are, they are). Its, your and their show belonging and never have an apostrophe.
steps: Try replacing the word with it is / you are / they are.
If the sentence still makes sense, use the apostrophe form.
If it doesn't, use its / your / their.
contractions_vs_possessives.sense_check: 'The cat licked it is paw' makes no sense, so it's 'its paw'.

steps: Try 'it is': the cat licked it is paw. No.

worked_examples.prompt: ___ going to love this book. (Your / You're)
steps: Try 'you are': You are going to love this book. Yes.
